title: Histological Insights into the Distribution of Immune Cells in the Esophagus in Koi Fish (Cyprinus rubrofuscus)
content:
Abstract
The esophagus of koi fish plays a critical role in digestion and immune defense, as it is directly exposed to a variety of pathogens. This study investigates the histological features and the immune cell composition and enrichment within the esophagus of koi fish, aiming to understand the local immune response mechanisms. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses were conducted on esophagus samples from koi fish, focusing on the distribution of various immune cells. Our results indicate a notable enrichment of immune cells (lymphocytes, macrophages, rodlet cell) in the esophageal mucosa. In addition, the presence of goblet cells, club cells, and telocytes suggests that they play a role in immune cell regulation. The study highlights the adaptive immune system's presence in this region and suggests that the esophagus may serve as a crucial site for mucosal immunity, offering a first line of defense against ingested pathogens through mechanical barriers and immune activation. Understanding the immune cell dynamics in the koi fish esophagus could provide insights into fish immunology and help improve aquaculture health management practices.
